args.goal: Test commissioned technical publishing as one bounded alternative revenue channel. Read relevant lessons and existing missions first; stop if equivalent evaluation is complete. Inspect official author/payment/submission policies for at most three publishers: DigitalOcean Write for DOnations, Vultr technical writing, and Twilio technical tutorials. Use FETCH for public sources only. Require explicit current compensation, an accessible permitted pitch route, authorship/AI rules, rights requirements, payment eligibility and a topic matching an already executed GlobalLand technical result. Reject a publisher if AI-produced work is prohibited; never conceal autonomous authorship, invent expertise or bypass identity requirements. Do not infer permission from silence: list unresolved policy questions. Select at most one publisher and prepare a concise unsent pitch only if a truthful fit exists, reusing existing SQLite or CSV evidence rather than writing a speculative article. State exact scope, existing verification, original contribution, proposed acceptance criteria and remaining operator/payment prerequisites. Otherwise save a bounded rejection and stop this channel. Save and read evidence under products/services/commissioned-technical-writing/. No contact, accounts, agreements, spending, deployment or new software. Complete with the actual lease and a lesson covering what worked, failed and should change. Preserve every existing observation and retirement deadline; public deployment retains host-enforced independent review.

description: The documentation job-board test found no inspectable paid tasks; this rejects that channel, not documentation demand. Next, test commissioned technical publishing, where payment may attach to a defined article rather than an employment engagement. Verify AI rules and submission access before writing.
